_comment: THE RELEASE MANIFEST. hexaeight-activate reads this to decide which release to install and what
it must hash to, so a new release is published by updating binaries and this file - not by
building and republishing the tool.
Two different hashes, answering two different questions:
sha256      the DOWNLOADED FILE. Checked before anything is executed.
protection  the EXTRACTED ENTRY ASSEMBLY, which is what a build attests on the wire, and what
a peer's approved-build gate matches on.
PROTECTION HASHES NO LONGER NEED A MACHINE OF THAT KIND. With PublishSingleFile plus
IncludeAllContentForSelfExtract the entry dll is embedded VERBATIM and UNCOMPRESSED in the
bundle - verified byte-for-byte - so what a platform extracts at first run is exactly the dll
the build produced. Hashing the build's own intermediate dll therefore yields the same value on
any host. Confirmed on linux-x64 by measuring both ways and getting one number, and the builds
are reproducible (two independent builds of r14 produced identical hashes).
That also retires the trap that made the old ceremony fragile: ~/.net/<exe-name>/ is keyed on
the EXECUTABLE FILENAME, which every release reuses, so it accumulates one directory per
release and 'newest by mtime' was a guess.
ENGINES ARE PUBLISHED HERE TOO, as engine-harness and engine-mindmapchat. They used to live
only inside HexaEight.Activate, which meant every engine rebuild required a nuget release - an
irreversible publish to ship a number about a file on GitHub, and a window in between where
install-agent downloaded a good binary and deleted it as unverified. An engine fix now ships
like an agent fix: new binaries, one commit here.
Editing this file changes what every installation fetches. Update the sha256 in the same commit
as the binary it describes.
